stories.title: Iran says it can reopen the Strait of Hormuz in two days as Gulf states brace for possible US strikes
stories.summary: Iran says it has shortened a plan to reopen the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] and resume nuclear talks with the United States from seven days to two, and describes its indirect talks with Washington as “intensive”, France 24 and Al Jazeera report. Qatar has led mediation for 72 hours to head off a possible new round of US attacks after Tuesday’s [[midterms|midterm elections]], NPR reports, leaving the Gulf region on edge. France 24 says Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to “finish the job”.
stories.background: The US and Israel went to war with Iran in early 2026, and Iran has since closed or restricted the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for the world’s oil. The US has a naval blockade on Iran. Iran says the talks rest on a seven-step plan it drew up in September.

stories.title: Americans vote on Tuesday in midterms that polls suggest could hand Democrats control of Congress
stories.summary: Voters choose on Tuesday in midterm elections that could flip one or both chambers of Congress from Republican to Democratic, France 24 says; it puts President Donald Trump’s approval rating at 32%. The Times of Israel reports that final polls see Democrat wins in all seven tight races. Trump is due to make a “closing argument” speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, The National reports. In Michigan, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the Senate, splitting Democrats, NPR reports.
stories.background: US midterm elections are held halfway through a president’s four-year term and decide all 435 House seats and about a third of the Senate. The party in the White House has usually lost seats in these votes.

stories.title: Russian bombs kill 24 at a Ukrainian aid centre as the war’s longest ceasefire ends
stories.summary: Russian bombing killed 24 people in a village in southern Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian emergency services say. President Volodymyr Zelensky says the first strike hit a school used as a humanitarian aid centre and nine more bombs then hit a shelter where people had taken refuge; the BBC says at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs were used. Zelensky says Russia is “sending an entirely opposite signal” to hopes of progress toward peace, Euronews reports. Separately, a six-day truce that let hundreds of people leave the occupied city of Oleshky has ended and fighting has returned to the Kherson region, the BBC says; the Kremlin has ruled out similar operations for now, according to the Kyiv Independent.
stories.background: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. US-mediated peace efforts have repeatedly stalled, and Moscow says the situation on the battlefield will decide when talks begin.

stories.title: Trump administration asks the Supreme Court to block 20,000 California ballots
stories.summary: The administration has appealed to the Supreme Court over claims that a list of more than 20,000 California ballots includes non-US citizens, DW reports, adding that multiple courts and independent analysis have rejected the claims. California says any move to block ballots from suspected noncitizens could disenfranchise eligible voters, Al Jazeera reports. Separately, a judge has dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit that sought to delay certifying Alaska’s Senate result if the Republican incumbent loses, the BBC reports.
stories.background: In the US, states run elections and count the ballots, and courts have often been asked to settle disputes just before or after a vote. The Supreme Court is the final court of appeal.

stories.title: Supermarket freezers in seven European countries hit by a second suspected cyber-attack
stories.summary: Supermarket chains in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden say cooling-unit temperatures rose overnight, France 24 and the Guardian report. The BBC says temperatures in some freezers reportedly climbed as high as 50C and dozens of shops dumped large amounts of food. It comes three weeks after a similar incident at French shops, DW says. Euronews cites new research finding nearly 13,000 refrigeration controls openly reachable online in 99 countries, many running outdated software. Neither the BBC nor the Guardian reports a confirmed culprit.
stories.background: Many fridges, heating systems and cameras are now connected to the internet so they can be monitored remotely. That convenience can also let attackers reach them if they are poorly secured.

stories.title: Cost-of-living protests spread across France and Germany, with school blockades and strikes
stories.summary: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against rising living costs and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police, the BBC reports; hundreds were arrested over the weekend and France has opened an attempted-murder investigation after a petrol bomb was thrown at police. In Germany, largely peaceful demonstrations turned to violence and looting in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, the BBC says, and unions have launched a wave of strikes over cost-of-living pressures, according to Al Jazeera. The Guardian reports dozens of French high schools were blockaded again on Monday and unions plan a nationwide strike on Thursday.
stories.background: French protests have been held on consecutive Saturdays since October, with tens of thousands of police deployed. Governments across Europe are under pressure from higher prices, which some link to the war involving Iran and the resulting fuel costs.

stories.title: Petition to take the French TV channel CNews off air passes 500,000 signatures
stories.summary: The petition passed half a million signatures on Monday after a Frenchman shot dead a French national of Congolese origin and wounded seven others, France 24 reports. DW says support surged after the shooting of a Black man by a reported avid viewer of CNews, and that critics describe the channel, often compared to Fox News, as a platform for anti-immigrant sentiment. Africanews reports that the family of the victim, Pengo Bossio Wangi, who was killed in a racist attack on 23 October near Paris, hopes for an “awakening” against racism in France.
stories.background: CNews is a right-wing French news channel. Calls to ban a broadcaster are rare in France, where media regulation is handled by an independent authority.

stories.title: Israel’s president starts coalition talks after a deadlocked election
stories.summary: President Isaac Herzog has begun coalition negotiations, France 24 reports; one possibility is for the centrist opposition bloc to form a government with Arab parties, which would oust the current government. The Times of Israel says Avigdor Liberman will back Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister but rules out a minority government with Arab support, while the Joint List chief says his party will not join a coalition but cites “awful 4 years” as a reason to help unseat Netanyahu. Netanyahu has defended Shas chair Aryeh Deri amid reports of a possible effort to oust him after a poor election showing.
stories.background: Israeli governments are formed by coalitions, because no party usually wins a majority of the 120 seats in the [[knesset|Knesset]]. The president asks the lawmaker with the best chance of assembling a majority to try.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill at least eight, hospitals say
stories.summary: Hospitals say Israeli strikes killed eight people, including a child, five of them officers of the Hamas-run police in Khan Younis, the BBC reports. The Israeli military says six Hamas operatives, two of them involved in the 7 October attack, were killed in recent strikes; it did not immediately comment on Monday’s strikes, which Palestinian sources say killed four, The Times of Israel reports.

stories.title: Oil falls to a two-week low on hopes of a breakthrough to end the Iran war
stories.summary: [[brent-crude|Brent crude]] dropped more than 6% to $105.55 a barrel, its lowest in more than two weeks, as hopes grew of a breakthrough to end the Iran war, the Guardian reports. High fuel costs are still biting: Ryanair says it may freeze workers’ pay and raise fares, warning fuel could cost €2bn more in 2028 unless the war ends, the BBC reports. US diesel eased to $6.29 a gallon, Al Jazeera says, and Pakistan cut diesel by Rs7.76 a litre and petrol by Rs3.40, according to Dawn. NPR reports a cruise line suspended an “endless cruise” citing soaring fuel costs, leaving passengers to disembark in Cambodia.
stories.background: Brent is the main international price benchmark for oil. Prices rose sharply after the war disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key export route.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 and is the fastest-growing on record, Euronews reports
stories.summary: Euronews reports that the outbreak, caused by the rare [[ebola-bundibugyo|Bundibugyo]] virus, has infected more than 10,000 people since May and has spread to Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria. The World Health Organization chief says recent Ebola and hantavirus outbreaks show why countries must finalise a pandemic treaty without delay. Premium Times says the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to raise concerns about regional health security.
stories.background: Ebola spreads through contact with the body fluids of infected people. Bundibugyo is a less common strain than Zaire ebolavirus, and fewer vaccines and treatments have been developed for it.

stories.title: Uganda starts pulling troops out of Somalia as UN missions in Somalia and Western Sahara end
stories.summary: Uganda has begun withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years, the BBC reports; they have helped Somalia fight the al-Shabab insurgency since 2007. DW says the mission has faced mounting pressure since a US decision to withdraw funding. The United Nations political mission in Somalia ended after a two-year transition, closing more than three decades of UN peace-building there, ThisDay reports via AllAfrica. NPR says the UN peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ceased operations on Sunday after 35 years; the territory is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.

stories.title: Spain identifies 66 of the 69 Urda train crash victims as drivers call new strikes
stories.summary: Authorities have identified 66 of the 69 people killed in the Urda collision and the government is to approve financial aid for those affected, The Local reports. Victims included four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic. The BBC reports a University of Cambridge scientist, Marta Shahbazi, was among the dead, and Mexico News Daily says a Mexican-born arts organiser from Oklahoma City, 45, also died. Train drivers have called two new stoppage days this month, The Local says.
stories.background: A Renfe high-speed train ran into the back of a stopped Iryo train, and Spain’s transport minister blamed “inexplicable human error”. It was the second major rail disaster in Spain this year.

stories.title: Cyclone Murasu nears India’s Andhra Pradesh coast with heavy rain across five states
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu is expected to make landfall near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh between Monday midnight and Tuesday morning, Scroll reports. The India Meteorological Department says winds of 100 to 110 km/h, gusting to 120 km/h, are likely between Nellore and Narasapur, The Hindu reports, and at least 19 domestic flights were cancelled at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam. Chennai schools were closed and the city had heavy rain, though The Times of India reports no widespread waterlogging. Murasu is the first Tamil name given to a tropical cyclone since naming began over the north Indian Ocean in 2004.
stories.background: Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal are named from a rotating list agreed by countries around the north Indian Ocean. Cyclone Arnab, which struck last week, was the previous storm in the series covered here.

stories.title: Opposition rally in Delhi demands the election chief resign as Amit Shah defends the voter-roll revision
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in central Delhi on Sunday, calling for the chief election commissioner to step down, the BBC reports. Home Minister Amit Shah has backed the [[sir|SIR]] voter-roll revision, calling about three crore of the voters dropped “infiltrators” who “never existed”, The Indian Express reports; The Hindu says he put the figure at three crore among 13 crore deleted voters, and Telangana minister Ponnam Prabhakar asked the BJP to say how many foreign nationals were identified. Delhi Police have registered an FIR against 22 protesters detained during a march towards Jantar Mantar. The Bombay High Court extended a stay on a “leave India” notice to actor Imran Khan, an OCI cardholder, after he apologised for joining the protest, Scroll reports.
stories.background: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is an Election Commission drive to re-verify voter rolls state by state. Opposition parties say it removes genuine voters; the government says it removes ineligible names.

stories.title: Delhi’s air turns ‘very poor’ as the Supreme Court allows green firecrackers for Diwali
stories.summary: Delhi’s air quality index rose from 117 on 31 October to 261 on 1 November and then 324, and Stage-II [[grap|GRAP]] curbs have been invoked, The Hindu reports; Scroll says three monitoring stations recorded “severe” readings above 400. The Supreme Court called Diwali fireworks a “religious practice” but noted that they cause severe pollution, and allowed green crackers from 6am to 8pm on 7 November and 7am to 10pm on 8 November. The Hindu found banned crackers sold under the counter in Sadar Bazar and near Jama Masjid, and police have seized more than 1,100 kg.
stories.background: Delhi’s air typically worsens each autumn as colder air traps pollution from vehicles, dust, crop-stubble burning and festival fireworks.
